title: Network capture analysed: 6 workload(s), 28 flow(s), 8 anomaly(ies)
description: policy_mode=audit egress=28 ingress=0 distinct_egress_dests=17 verdict_allow=23 verdict_deny=5 bytes_tx=62919956 bytes_rx=12812

title: No default-deny egress policy in effect
description: The capture ran with policy_mode="audit" while workloads made outbound connections. Without a default-deny egress baseline, a compromised workload can reach any destination (C2, exfil, IMDS).
remediation: Apply a namespace-wide default-deny egress NetworkPolicy, then allow only observed destinations. Generate both with: dsecrat net <capture> --gen deny  and  dsecrat net <capture> --gen policy

title: Egress to cloud instance-metadata endpoint (IMDS)
description: Workload "prod/malware" connected to metadata endpoint 169.254.169.254 3 time(s). This endpoint vends node/instance IAM credentials; container access to it is a common credential-theft and privilege-escalation path.
remediation: Block egress to 169.254.169.254 for this workload and enforce IMDSv2 (hop-limit 1). Generate the deny with: dsecrat net <capture> --gen deny --workload prod/malware

title: Periodic C2 beaconing pattern to external host
description: 6 connections to cdn.evil-c2.example at a near-constant 60s interval (jitter CV 0.000), averaging 512 bytes each — the low-jitter, low-volume signature of an automated callback.
remediation: Confirm the destination is legitimate; if not, isolate the workload and restrict egress to the generated least-privilege allowlist: dsecrat net <capture> --gen fqdn --workload prod/malware

title: Probable DGA activity (NXDOMAIN storm to high-entropy domains)
description: 12 NXDOMAIN responses across 12 distinct parent domains with avg leftmost-label entropy 3.84 bits/char — the pattern of a domain-generation algorithm probing for its live C2 rendezvous.
remediation: Confirm the destination is legitimate; if not, isolate the workload and restrict egress to the generated least-privilege allowlist: dsecrat net <capture> --gen fqdn --workload prod/dga-bot

title: Probable DNS tunnelling (high-entropy subdomain queries)
description: 25 queries under "tunnel.example" with avg subdomain entropy 3.94 bits/char and avg length 24 (max 24); 25 used data-carrying record types. Long, high-entropy labels under one parent are the signature of DNS tunnelling.
remediation: Confirm the destination is legitimate; if not, isolate the workload and restrict egress to the generated least-privilege allowlist: dsecrat net <capture> --gen fqdn --workload prod/dns-tunnel

title: High-volume upload to external host (possible data exfiltration)
description: Workload "prod/malware" sent 60.0 MiB to drop.exfil-store.example across 1 connection(s) with a 15360.0:1 upload:download ratio — an upload-dominant transfer to a single external destination.
remediation: Confirm the destination is legitimate; if not, isolate the workload and restrict egress to the generated least-privilege allowlist: dsecrat net <capture> --gen fqdn --workload prod/malware

title: Lateral-movement fan-out across internal peers
description: Workload "prod/scanner" connected to 12 distinct internal peers across 12 distinct port(s) — a fan-out consistent with east-west scanning or lateral movement rather than a fixed dependency set.
remediation: Apply identity/label-based east-west segmentation so this workload can only reach its known dependencies. Generate a NetworkPolicy: dsecrat net <capture> --gen policy --workload prod/scanner

title: Workload runs with host network namespace
description: hostNetwork removes network-namespace isolation; NetworkPolicy/egress rules do not apply to this pod.
remediation: Remove hostNetwork:true unless strictly required; host-networked pods bypass NetworkPolicy and cannot be egress-contained.

title: Egress denied by policy (blocked-egress alert)
description: 5 egress attempt(s) from "prod/blocked-app" to blocked.example were dropped by policy. Repeated denials can indicate a misconfigured allowlist or a workload probing for an exit.
remediation: Review the flow against the workload's intended egress baseline and add an explicit allow or deny rule.
